clue.text: Charm of parent's bed

blocks.note: MA is a mother, a parent, with the possessive 's kept
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A good-luck token taken from a mother's or father's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, an object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Playful mischief from maiden who's a guest at a wonderful tea party?

blocks.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

blocks.clueFragment: who's a guest at a wonderful tea party?
blocks.note: Alice joins the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A young woman at an odd tea party causing light-hearted trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonderful' points to Wonderland, the setting of the Mad Hatter's tea party that Alice attends.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is usually ill will, but the setter leans on the teasing, mock-wicked sense of a mischievous glint.

clue.text: Kent/Sussex area with channel showing Coast

blocks.note: Kent and Sussex lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
A is the standard abbreviation for area
'side' is old British informal for a TV channel, as in 'switch over to the other side'

explanation.surface: A South East England region beside the English Channel shows off its coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like the English Channel but is a television channel; Kent and Sussex are counties in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coast, the land along the sea where people go on holiday.

clue.text: Postponed over fine

blocks.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
nice and fine both mean pleasant or satisfactory

explanation.surface: Something delayed because of an issue about a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are suspended or deferred until later, an idiom from keeping food cold.

clue.text: Play the part in current hype

blocks.note: AC is alternating current
to tout is to promote or hype something

explanation.surface: An actor taking a role in the latest publicity campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a scene is to perform it, playing the role as if on stage.

clue.text: It's bound to work as one group quip about beginning from nine

definitions.text: It's bound to work as one

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other
'beginning from' keeps only the first letter of 'nine'

blocks.note: a chain is a group of shops or hotels under one owner
a gag is a joke
the first letter of nine

explanation.surface: A team bound to work together, joking from the start of its nine o'clock shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One group' reads as a single phrase, but 'as one' ends the definition and 'group' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain gang is a team of prisoners shackled together while doing labour, literally bound to work in unison.

clue.text: Opening scripture studies for foremost female in service

indicators.note: one thing given for another is a swap, so a piece takes another letter's place

blocks.note: an office is a religious service, as in the Divine Office
RI is Religious Instruction, the old school subject
the first letter of female, the one taken out

explanation.surface: Scripture study opening up for the leading woman in a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: The first F of OFFICE is replaced by RI; F is the first letter of 'female'.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or opening, especially one in the body.

clue.text: Mess that's most frequently seen in tight corner

indicators.note: asks which letter occurs most often in the following word, the only one appearing twice

blocks.note: T appears twice in tight, more often than any other letter
an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: A predicament most commonly met when stuck in a difficult position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight corner' reads as one idiom for a predicament; split, 'tight' supplies its most common letter and 'corner' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a confused, knotted mess, as of string or hair.

clue.text: This is left after burning tree

blocks.note: first meaning: the powdery residue of a fire
second meaning: a common deciduous tree

explanation.surface: A tree's remains after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the residue left by combustion and a familiar tree of the olive family.

clue.text: Sadly fearless tones make others sit up and listen

definitions.text: make others sit up and listen

indicators.note: things going sadly are going badly, so these letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Bold voices, unfortunately, are what get people's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert oneself is to behave confidently and forcefully, which compels others to take notice.

clue.text: Board keep standing for a well-known celeb?

blocks.note: to board someone is to lodge or house them
to keep is to hold
standing in the sense of reputation, a good name

explanation.surface: A company board keeping its position on behalf of a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a noun, a committee, but works as a verb meaning provide lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A household name is a person so famous that everyone at home knows them; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Starts endless low grade rows

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: lean ore is low-grade ore, poor in metal
rows as in noisy quarrels, rhyming with cows; dins are loud noises

explanation.surface: Low-quality arguments that begin and never stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' reads like lines but means rackets; 'low grade' is a mining term for poor ore, which is called lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead-ins are introductions, the openings that lead into a programme or piece.

clue.text: Nothing helping address

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A speech that is of no help at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, an address delivered to an audience.

clue.text: What is the focus for Detective Frost?

definitions.text: What is the focus for Detective Frost?

indicators.note: the focus of something is its centre, so the middle letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the central letter of the nine-letter word detective
rime is hoar frost, ice crystals formed on cold surfaces

explanation.surface: Asking what a TV detective named Frost spends his time investigating.
explanation.walkthrough: Detective Inspector Jack Frost is the hero of the British TV police drama A Touch of Frost; read whole, the clue asks what he investigates, which is also the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective's job is investigating offences against the law, so wrongdoing is where Frost's attention lies.

clue.text: Formal lease isn't to be broken

indicators.note: something broken falls into pieces that can be put back in another order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An official tenancy agreement must not be violated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formal' is used in its philosophical sense, concerning the form or essence of a thing, not its everyday sense of ceremonious.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy, formal means relating to a thing's essence rather than its matter, so it equals essential.

clue.text: Fleeced outside function when purchasing that bloke's ecstasy

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the first word wraps the next
purchasing means taking in or acquiring, so the same word also holds a second piece

blocks.note: a fleeced sheep has been shorn, or shaven
a function is a social event
the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A man fleeced at a party while buying himself some drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' means while the outer word does something, letting one word hold two separate pieces. 'Ecstasy' looks like the drug but is bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventh heaven is a state of utter happiness, from the highest of the heavens in some traditions.

clue.text: So among classicists

indicators.note: among means sitting in the middle of others, so the answer lies inside the next word

blocks.note: the run of letters after the first four of this word

explanation.surface: A remark about how scholars of Latin and Greek say 'thus'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the Latin translation of 'so', which is indeed the answer, a neat touch since classicists use Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sic is Latin for thus, used in brackets to show quoted wording is reproduced exactly as in the original.

clue.text: Bring to the fore new pie and mash store being vacant

indicators.note: a vacant word is emptied of its inside, leaving only its two ends
a new version of something is a remade one, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the outside letters of store

explanation.surface: A newly opened pie and mash shop, standing empty, wants to promote itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie and mash is a traditional London working-class meal, sold in dedicated shops.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise something is to give it prominence, bringing it to the foreground of attention.

clue.text: This oddball overturned barrel

indicators.note: turned over, so in a down entry the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: An eccentric knocks over a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is informal for a crazy or eccentric person, the same as an oddball.

clue.text: Affected by an academic ironically I'll ring the changes

blocks.note: camp means theatrically affected or exaggerated
taken as written
an -ologist is a jokey name for any expert, said with irony

explanation.surface: A pretentious scholar announces, with irony, that he will make some alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring the changes' sounds like an idiom for varying things, but here it is literal: ringing changes is the bellringer's art.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanologist is a bell-ringer, and ringing changes means pulling bells in varying orders.

clue.text: Flying service is excellent, bar getting miles in

indicators.note: getting here means receiving something inside, so one piece is put into another

blocks.note: A1 means first-class; crosswords write it with the letter I
a rail is a bar
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A top-rate flight service, except when it racks up mileage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like 'except' but is a rod, the M going in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is the postal service carrying letters by aircraft.

clue.text: A little scam supporting starter often

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece holds up the other, so it comes below it

blocks.note: soup is often served as a first course
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A small fraud underpinning a frequent opening move.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a very small amount, a trace or hint, borrowed from French.

clue.text: A woman who inspires daughter is tickled pink

blocks.note: taken as written
a muse is a woman who inspires an artist
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter's inspiring woman is delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickled pink means greatly entertained or delighted, so amused fits as a past participle.

clue.text: Late split trapping Chancellor of the Exchequer

indicators.note: trapping means holding something inside, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: rent is the past tense of rend, to tear apart
CE is the abbreviation for Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister

explanation.surface: The late finance minister caught in a political split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like 'deceased' in the surface but means not long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the sense of 'of late' means recent, lately happened.

clue.text: Moralist troubled by indefinite number showing loss of grace or inebriety?

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and unsettled, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A moralist upset by countless instances of fallen behaviour or drunkenness.
explanation.walkthrough: In Catholic teaching a grave sin causes the loss of sanctifying grace; the question mark nods to British 'mortal' meaning blind drunk, so drinking is a 'mortal' sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal sin is a grave sin that destroys the state of grace in the soul.

clue.text: Constant unrefined oil

blocks.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
rude means coarse or unpolished

explanation.surface: Oil that is always unprocessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrefined oil' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'oil' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude is petroleum in its natural unprocessed state, short for crude oil.

clue.text: Pink pen having only one nib to replace

indicators.text: having only one nib to replace
indicators.note: where two identical points sit side by side, keeping just one means the duplicate is dropped

blocks.note: a corral is an animal pen

explanation.surface: A pink pen that needs just one new nib.
explanation.walkthrough: The writing pen is really an enclosure for livestock; of its doubled R only one survives.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour, named after the marine growth.

clue.text: Dog leaps in playfully

indicators.note: playing about with letters jumbles them into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dog jumps in for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of dog with long drooping ears, such as the cocker.

clue.text: Wonder if unit captures reversing vehicle

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word is read right to left
to capture is to take inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a mile is a unit of distance
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an army unit will seize a vehicle backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is a marvel, something that causes wonder.

clue.text: Green group, a rival of backing energy?

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word before it is read the other way

blocks.note: the little word written back to front
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An environmental group, rival of a backer of energy?
explanation.walkthrough: FOE is Friends of the Earth, a campaigning environmental group; the clue gives this and a second definition, then wordplay too.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe is an enemy or opponent, and Friends of the Earth is abbreviated FoE.

clue.text: Comparatively slow fighter short of first base

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so something is taken away

blocks.note: a dueller fights duels
E is the base of natural logarithms; the first of its two appearances goes

explanation.surface: A baseball player who is slower than others, never reaching first base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First base' sounds like baseball, but base is the maths constant e, and it is the first of the two Es in the fighter that is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull can mean slow-witted, so duller is the comparative, slower to grasp things.

clue.text: Craft heading to Third World

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a plane is an aircraft
the first letter of third

explanation.surface: An aircraft bound for the developing nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third World' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'World' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a world, a large body orbiting a star.
